use /lib
from /scope/harness-integration import HarnessIntegrationScope
from /scope/project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope
from /scope/lsp import LSP

export scope ChatInputScope:
    concept: {ChatInputConcept}

concept ChatInputConcept:
    pitch:
        A multi-line, syntax-highlighted textbox that accepts plain text as well
        as snippets of Piton.

    shape: {ChatInputShape}

shape ChatInputShape:
    description:
        Input on the left, send button on the right.

        <Enter> allows for creating new lines, like Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends it to
        the ${HarnessIntegrationScope}

        Sending is never blocked by the harness working: while it is, the send
        button reads "Queue" and sending adds the prompt to prompt mode's
        queue. The button is only disabled while the input is empty.

    tabs:
        overview:
            The input and send button live inside the body of a tab bar, using
            gpui-kit's default tab styling. The two tabs are Code and Spec,
            with a chain button between them that selects both, reading
            "Code and Spec" as its tooltip.

            Pressing <Tab> while in the chat input cycles from Code to the
            chain to Spec and back to Code, <Shift+Tab> the other way, and
            focus remains in the chat input.

        chain:
            A small square button, half the height of the tabs and vertically
            centred on them, with no focus border.

            Inactive, it shows a broken chain dimmed to 50% opacity, and
            Code and Spec sit apart with a gap between them wide enough that
            the chain sits in the gap without overlapping either tab.

            Active, it shows a joined chain at full opacity, both tabs are
            selected, and Code and Spec animate closer together until they
            meet beneath the chain, which overlaps both and covers the seam
            so they read as one locked tab. Deactivating it animates them
            apart again.

            The chain never moves: it stays at the same place in both states,
            and only the tabs slide toward or away from it.

    systemPrompt:
        The selected tab is the mode a prompt is sent in, and each mode gives
        the hidden anchor a systemPrompt property alongside its userPrompt.
        The code location is `codeRoot` and the spec location is `root`, as
        set in the project's piton.config.pi.

        code:
            We're working on the code located in <code location>. Don't edit
            the spec located in <spec location>.

        spec:
            We're working on the spec located in <spec location>. Don't edit
            the code located in <code location>.

        both:
            We're working on both the code located in <code location> and the
            spec located in <spec location>. Edit both of them.

        A prompt keeps the mode it was sent in while it waits in the queue.

    escape:
        Pressing <Escape> while in the chat input takes focus out of the chat
        input.

    growToFit:
        The text input will grow to fit the text inside of it, one row per
        visual line: both lines broken with <Enter> and long lines that soft
        wrap. It shrinks again as text is removed, and re-fits when the window
        is resized. It starts at a single row, lined up with the send button,
        and stops growing at 12 rows, after which it scrolls.

    autoFocus:
        The chat input should be auto-focused.

    syntaxHighlighting:
        Syntax highlighting will be supported via the [Tree Sitter
        Grammar](https://github.com/piton-lang/tree-sitter-piton)

    lsp: @{LSP}

    harnessMentions:
        overview:
            Typing `/` offers the harness's skills and commands, and typing `@`
            offers its agents, the way they are offered in the harness itself.
            The placeholder mentions both.

        trigger:
            A mention starts at `/` or `@` at the start of the input or after
            whitespace, so paths and email addresses never open it, and an at sign
            followed by an opening curly brace is still a Piton reference. Completions are
            requested after typing the `/` or `@`, and after each letter,
            digit, hyphen, underscore, or colon of the name that follows. Only
            inside a mention are a slash or a hyphen a trigger; outside of one
            they never reach the @{LSP}.

        offered:
            Skills and commands are those of the selected
            ${ProjectDirectoryScope}, of the user, and of the user's enabled
            plugins, a plugin's own being named `plugin:name`. Agents come from
            the same places, plus the harness's built-in agents. Each shows
            whether it is a skill, command, or agent, and its description as
            documentation when it has one. Every harness run reports the skills
            and agents it has, built-in ones included; the last report is saved
            with the project and offered too. Results are narrowed and ordered
            like Piton completions: matches at the start of a name before
            matches anywhere in it, then by name.

        accepting:
            Accepting a skill or command inserts `/name `, and accepting an
            agent inserts `@agent-name `, which the harness understands as a
            request to use that agent. They pass through the hidden anchor and
            its compilation unchanged, so a prompt starting with `/name` runs
            that skill or command. Mentions work without the @{LSP}.

    hiddenAnchor:
        While the user will be able to type plain text, behind the scenes,
        they'll be typing into a randomly-named piton anchor with a userPrompt
        property.  It's this compiled anchor that will be send to the
        @{HarnessIntegrationScope}

content.content:
# Piton fluency

Piton is a declarative, whitespace-structured language for describing agentic
skills, agents, commands, and reference documents. It has no runtime: it
compiles to data (JSON, YAML) or, through a framework, to Markdown. Source
files use the `.pi` extension.

## Syntax

```piton
// A comment. Comments are line-only.
myVariable: 42                       // a number
myString: Strings are unquoted       // a string
myQuoted: "false"                    // quoting forces a string
myTyped:: string:: number: 42        // constraints, first match wins

myList:
    - one
    - two
myInlineList: [one, two, three]

myDictionary:
    nested:
        deep: value

computed: {1 + 2}                    // `{ }` evaluates; bare text does not
interpolated: Hello, ${myString}

anchor Base:
    name: Base
    summary: This is ${this.name}  // `this` pins to Base

anchor Child extends Base:
    name: Child
    detail: This is ${self.name}   // `self` follows the child
    summary: ${super.summary} and more

abstract anchor Shape as shape:      // `as` registers a keyword
    description:: string

shape Concrete:                      // same as `extends Shape`
    description: Implemented

from ./other import Thing, Other Alias
from ./other export *
use ./keywords
export anchor Published:
    value: 1
```

## Reserved words

`anchor`, `abstract`, `extends`, `as`, `export`, `from`, `import`, `use`, `this`, `self`, `super`, `true`, `false`, `null`

## Types

`string`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`, `list`, `dictionary`, `anchor`, `any`, `simple`, `complex`

Literals: `true`, `false`, `null`

## Rules worth memorising

- A value is an expression only when the *whole* value parses as one over
  literal atoms. `1 + 2` is `3`; `a + b` is the string `a + b`; use `{a + b}`
  to reference names.
- `+` on lists concatenates and deduplicates, right operand winning:
  `[1,2,3,4] + [1,2,3]` is `[4,1,2,3]`. `++` keeps duplicates.
- `+` merges dictionaries shallowly; `++` merges them deeply.
- Mixing unrelated types with `+` produces a mixed list, not an error.
- A block that mixes prose, `- ` items, and `key:` pairs becomes an implicit
  list; the keys written directly in it stay addressable.
- Inheritance is left to right with the right-most base winning; a child always
  wins over its bases; a declaring keyword is the left-most base.
- A concrete anchor may implement at most one abstract anchor, and must supply
  every abstract property left without a value.
- Strings never coerce to `boolean` or `number`; simple values do coerce to
  `string`.
- Modulo uses floor semantics; division by zero and comparing mismatched types
  are compile errors.
- Two files may import from each other. A circular reference is an error only
  when it cannot settle: `${A}` and `${B}` naming each other is fine, because an
  interpolated anchor renders as its name, while `A: {B}` and `B: {A}` is not.
- Indentation must be consistent within a file; the canonical style is four
  spaces.

## Frameworks

### `@piton/belay` (framework `belay`)

`use @piton/belay` for its keywords, `from @piton/belay import ...` for its anchors.

Interpolation sigils: `@{}`

- **Agent** (abstract anchor) — keyword `agent`
  - `description:: string`
  - `role:: string`
  - `prompt:: string`
- **Skill** (abstract anchor) — keyword `skill`
  - `description:: string`
  - `prompt:: string`
  - `useWhen:: string`
- **Command** (abstract anchor) — keyword `command`
  - `description:: string`
  - `prompt:: string`
- **Instruction** (abstract anchor) — keyword `instruction`
  - `description:: string`
  - `prompt:: string`
- **SelfInstruction** (abstract anchor) — keyword `self-instruction`
  - `description:: string`
  - `prompt:: string`
- **BelayConfig** (abstract anchor) — keyword `belay-config`
  - `codeRoot:: string`
- **Adapter** (abstract anchor) — keyword `belay-adapter`
  - `description:: string`
- **AgentAdapter** (abstract anchor) — keyword `belay-agent-adapter`
  - `description:: string`
- **ClaudeAdapter** (anchor)
  - `description`
  - `claude`
- **OpenCodeAdapter** (anchor)
  - `description`
  - `opencode`
- **__BELAY_SHAPE__** (variable)

## Working with a Piton project

- `piton check <glob>` reports errors without writing anything.
- `piton compile <glob>` writes JSON or YAML next to each input.
- `piton build` builds the project described by `piton.config.pi`.
- `piton build check` builds and reports without writing.
- `piton format <glob>` applies the canonical style: four spaces, one space
  after `//`, sorted and wrapped import lists.
- `piton lsp` runs the language server.

## Writing Piton well

- Prefer an abstract anchor exported `as` a keyword for anything that will be
  implemented repeatedly; it documents intent and prevents a concrete anchor
  from implementing two abstracts.
- Reach for `+ {super.x}` rather than repeating a base's list.
- Use `this` when a base wants its own value and `self` when it wants the
  most-derived one.
- Keep prose as prose. Only reach for `{ }` when a value genuinely needs to be
  computed or referenced.

use /lib
from /scope/harness-integration import HarnessIntegrationScope
from /scope/project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope
from /scope/lsp import LSP

export scope ChatInputScope:
    concept: {ChatInputConcept}

concept ChatInputConcept:
    pitch:
        A multi-line, syntax-highlighted textbox that accepts plain text as well
        as snippets of Piton.

    shape: {ChatInputShape}

shape ChatInputShape:
    description:
        Input on the left, send button on the right.

        <Enter> allows for creating new lines, like Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends it to
        the ${HarnessIntegrationScope}

        Sending is never blocked by the harness working: while it is, the send
        button reads "Queue" and sending adds the prompt to prompt mode's
        queue. The button is only disabled while the input is empty.

    tabs:
        overview:
            The input and send button live inside the body of a tab bar, using
            gpui-kit's default tab styling. The two tabs are Code and Spec,
            with a chain button between them that selects both, reading
            "Code and Spec" as its tooltip.

            Pressing <Tab> while in the chat input cycles from Code to the
            chain to Spec and back to Code, <Shift+Tab> the other way, and
            focus remains in the chat input.

        chain:
            A small square button, half the height of the tabs and vertically
            centred on them, with no focus border.

            Inactive, it shows a broken chain dimmed to 50% opacity, and
            Code and Spec sit apart with a gap between them wide enough that
            the chain sits in the gap without overlapping either tab.

            Active, it shows a joined chain at full opacity, both tabs are
            selected, and Code and Spec animate closer together until they
            meet beneath the chain, which overlaps both and covers the seam
            so they read as one locked tab. Deactivating it animates them
            apart again.

            The chain never moves: it stays at the same place in both states,
            and only the tabs slide toward or away from it.

    systemPrompt:
        The selected tab is the mode a prompt is sent in, and each mode gives
        the hidden anchor a systemPrompt property alongside its userPrompt.
        The code location is `codeRoot` and the spec location is `root`, as
        set in the project's piton.config.pi.

        code:
            We're working on the code located in <code location>. Don't edit
            the spec located in <spec location>.

        spec:
            We're working on the spec located in <spec location>. Don't edit
            the code located in <code location>.

        both:
            We're working on both the code located in <code location> and the
            spec located in <spec location>. Edit both of them.

        A prompt keeps the mode it was sent in while it waits in the queue.

    escape:
        Pressing <Escape> while in the chat input takes focus out of the chat
        input.

    growToFit:
        The text input will grow to fit the text inside of it, one row per
        visual line: both lines broken with <Enter> and long lines that soft
        wrap. It shrinks again as text is removed, and re-fits when the window
        is resized. It starts at a single row, lined up with the send button,
        and stops growing at 12 rows, after which it scrolls.

    autoFocus:
        The chat input should be auto-focused.

    syntaxHighlighting:
        Syntax highlighting will be supported via the [Tree Sitter
        Grammar](https://github.com/piton-lang/tree-sitter-piton)

    lsp: @{LSP}

    harnessMentions:
        overview:
            Typing `/` offers the harness's skills and commands, and typing `@`
            offers its agents, the way they are offered in the harness itself.
            The placeholder mentions both.

        trigger:
            A mention starts at `/` or `@` at the start of the input or after
            whitespace, so paths and email addresses never open it, and an at sign
            followed by an opening curly brace is still a Piton reference. Completions are
            requested after typing the `/` or `@`, and after each letter,
            digit, hyphen, underscore, or colon of the name that follows. Only
            inside a mention are a slash or a hyphen a trigger; outside of one
            they never reach the @{LSP}.

        offered:
            Skills and commands are those of the selected
            ${ProjectDirectoryScope}, of the user, and of the user's enabled
            plugins, a plugin's own being named `plugin:name`. Agents come from
            the same places, plus the harness's built-in agents. Each shows
            whether it is a skill, command, or agent, and its description as
            documentation when it has one. Every harness run reports the skills
            and agents it has, built-in ones included; the last report is saved
            with the project and offered too. Results are narrowed and ordered
            like Piton completions: matches at the start of a name before
            matches anywhere in it, then by name.

        accepting:
            Accepting a skill or command inserts `/name `, and accepting an
            agent inserts `@agent-name `, which the harness understands as a
            request to use that agent. They pass through the hidden anchor and
            its compilation unchanged, so a prompt starting with `/name` runs
            that skill or command. Mentions work without the @{LSP}.

    hiddenAnchor:
        While the user will be able to type plain text, behind the scenes,
        they'll be typing into a randomly-named piton anchor with a userPrompt
        property.  It's this compiled anchor that will be send to the
        @{HarnessIntegrationScope}

content.text:
I rewrote the tab section of `spec/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.pi` so Chain is a real tab, and `piton check` passes on the file. I didn't touch anything in `./src`.

- **Tabs:** There are now three tabs in order: Code, Chain and Spec. All three use the normal tab layout, size and spacing, with no extra gap around Chain. <Tab> and <Shift+Tab> still cycle through them.
- **What's different about Chain:** it shows an icon instead of a label, has "Code and Spec" as its tooltip, and selecting it selects both Code and Spec.
  - Unselected, it shows a broken chain at 50% opacity.
  - Selected, it shows a joined chain at full opacity, and all three tabs show as selected so they read as one locked tab.

**Removed:** the old layout only worked with a gap, so these rules are gone:
- Chain as a small square button, half the tab height, with no focus border.
- Code and Spec sliding together underneath a chain that never moves.

If you want an animation when Chain is selected, I can add one that works with tabs sitting flush against each other.
